newsitem.title: SPAIN: Strict Spain budget increases monetary scope - Rojo.
newsitem.headline: Strict Spain budget increases monetary scope - Rojo.

text.p: Bank of Spain governor Luis Angel Rojo said on Wednesday that the approval of a strict 1997 budget would increase the scope for manoeuvre in monetary policy.

"Approval of a budget which responds to expectations of reaching the Maastricht criteria for public deficit..will have a very positive effect on the money and financial markets and will increase the margin for monetary policy to more easily reach the forecast for inflation targets," Rojo said in a speech to a legislative economic committee.
He said that up to now Spain had used its interest rate scope gingerly to safeguard its fight against inflation.
"This difficulty (of fighting inflation) explains the Bank of Spain's prudence in administering the scope available to reduce its interest rates," Rojo said.
The Bank of Spain has reduced its key money market rate to 7.25 percent now from nine percent at the beginning of the year.
